title: Automated aDNA Extraction from Human Teeth
author: Allysson Farias
materials: Decontamination of consumables, reagents, and hood surface Expose all tubes, pipette tips, and reagents to UV light for 00:15:00 Place two sheets of aluminum foil on the work surface and irradiate both sides with UV light for 00:15:00 each side.

steps.title: Don personal protective equipment
steps.instruction: Remove personal items, tie long hair, perform hand hygiene with soap and water or 70 % alcohol, dry hands, put on shoe covers, disposable cap, 3M Aura 9320 respirator (seal check), wide‑vision goggles, and nitrile gloves (double‑glove, change outer pair between samples).

steps.title: Prepare clean room and work area
steps.instruction: Clean the BSL‑2 clean room using bleach solution (e.g., sodium hypochlorite) or an oxidising agent such as hydrogen peroxide; aseptically wipe all materials and surfaces with 70 % volume ethanol and gauze before and after use; separate the aluminium‑foil sheets that will cover the laminar‑flow hood.

steps.title: Decontaminate tooth samples
steps.instruction: Place each tooth in a labelled container under a mobile UV lamp, clean the tooth surface with gauze and bleach solution (do not remove calculus), irradiate each side for 15 min, and stay out of the room during UV exposure to avoid re‑contamination.

steps.title: Decontaminate dental drill head
steps.instruction: Clean all dental drills and drill heads with bleach and UV for 15 min, then detach each head and immerse it in fresh bleach solution in a beaker; clean each head separately for each new sample and never reuse bleach between samples.

steps.title: Decontaminate biosafety cabinet
steps.instruction: Wipe the biological safety cabinet with 70 % volume ethanol, turn on the UV lamp and irradiate the cabinet for 15 min.

steps.title: Prepare work surface and utensils
steps.instruction: Turn off the cabinet UV lamp, cover the work surface with one aluminium‑foil sheet and wipe it with 70 % ethanol, clean all utensils with high‑quality paper moistened with 70 % ethanol, place the cleaned utensils on the foil inside the cabinet, turn the UV lamp back on and irradiate the surface and utensils for 15 min until completely dry; repeat for each sample to be pulverised.

steps.title: Pulverise tooth to collect powder
steps.instruction: With the cabinet UV lamp off, place the archaeological tooth on the aluminium foil inside the cabinet, attach the drill head to the dental drill, drill at low RPM to generate approximately 100–150 mg of white powder, transfer the powder to a low‑retention microtube, label the tube with the sample ID and avoid overheating.

steps.title: Weigh and store bone powder
steps.instruction: Remove the microtube containing the powder from the cabinet, transfer the powder with a small spatula previously cleaned with 70 % ethanol (Step 3) to a second low‑retention microtube, weigh out exactly 10 mg using a precision balance with a glass enclosure, ensure the second tube is labelled, and store the first tube (remaining powder) at room temperature.

steps.title: Add DB3 buffer to powder
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL of DB3 buffer to each microtube that contains 10 mg of bone powder; verify that all tubes are correctly identified.

steps.title: Open extraction plates
steps.instruction: Open the plastic packaging of the extraction plates supplied with the kits; two extraction plates (one MPTA‑MDx and one MCFD) must be opened and used.

steps.title: Load samples onto MPTA-MDx plate
steps.instruction: Using the MPTA‑MDx extraction plate, add 300 µL of each sample to a single well, loading up to eight wells (one full column) for eight samples; add 20 µL of Proteinase K to each used well and change the pipette tip between samples.

steps.title: Load samples onto MCFD plate
steps.instruction: Using the MCFD extraction plate, add 300 µL of each sample to the wells of columns 1 and 2 (total 16 wells for eight samples); add 20 µL of Proteinase K and 6 µL of CR reagent to each used well.

steps.title: Incubate extraction plates
steps.instruction: Incubate both extraction plates at room temperature for an overnight period of 48 hours.

steps.title: Automated DNA extraction
steps.instruction: After incubation, place the two extraction plates into the Extracta 32 automated extractor (Loccus) and run the appropriate protocols: MPTAP016MDx for the MPTA‑MDx plate and MCFDP016 for the MCFD plate.

steps.title: Recover extracted DNA
steps.instruction: When the automated program finishes, remove the plates from the Extracta 32 and transfer the extracted DNA from each well into new, sterile, properly labelled microcentrifuge tubes.

steps.title: Thaw DNA samples
steps.instruction: On the day following extraction, remove the DNA tubes from the freezer, allow them to thaw at room temperature for 15 min, and continue all procedures wearing a lab coat, cap and nitrile gloves.

steps.title: Calibrate NanoDrop spectrophotometer
steps.instruction: Turn on the NanoDrop, place 1 µL ultrapure water on the pedestal, run a blank measurement, then clean the arm tip and pedestal with a high‑absorbency wipe; clean the pedestal between each subsequent measurement.

steps.title: Quantify DNA concentration
steps.instruction: Pipette 1 µL of a DNA sample onto the NanoDrop pedestal, click Measure to obtain concentration and absorbance ratios, clean the pedestal after each measurement, repeat for all 16 samples and repeat the entire quantification three times per sample.
